= Module 4: OpenAPI and Swagger UI
:source-highlighter: rouge
:toc: macro
:toclevels: 1

The Hero service is now operational with its CRUD operations. But OpenCodeQuest Corp needs the API to be documented so that other teams can use it. Quarkus automatically exposes an **OpenAPI** specification and an interactive **Swagger UI** -- with no additional configuration.

== Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you will be able to:

* Access the OpenAPI specification automatically generated by Quarkus
* Use Swagger UI to interactively explore and test the Hero API
* Locate the API in the Red Hat Developer Hub catalog

== Exercise 1: Access the OpenAPI specification

Quarkus includes the SmallRye OpenAPI extension compliant with the Eclipse MicroProfile OpenAPI specification. It automatically generates your API description in YAML/JSON format.

NOTE: The OpenAPI extension is already present in your `pom.xml` -- check for `quarkus-smallrye-openapi`.

. With the application running in Dev Mode (`quarkus dev`), in a Dev Spaces terminal, run:
+
[source,bash]
----
curl http://localhost:8080/q/openapi
----

. You should get the OpenAPI specification of your API:
+
[source,yaml]
----
---
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: hero-service API
  version: 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT
paths:
  /api/heroes:
    get:
      tags:
      - Hero Resource
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: "#/components/schemas/Hero"
    post:
      ...
  /api/heroes/hello:
    get:
      ...
  /api/heroes/random:
    get:
      ...
  /api/heroes/{id}:
    get:
      ...
    delete:
      ...
components:
  schemas:
    Hero:
      required:
      - name
      - level
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          format: int64
          type: integer
        name:
          maxLength: 50
          minLength: 3
          type: string
        level:
          format: int32
          minimum: 1
          type: integer
        picture:
          type: string
        powers:
          type: string
----
+
NOTE: Notice that Bean Validation constraints (`@Size`, `@Min`) are automatically reflected in the OpenAPI schema (`maxLength: 50`, `minimum: 1`).

=== Verify

✓ `curl /q/openapi` returns valid YAML describing all your endpoints

== Exercise 2: Explore the API with Swagger UI

Swagger UI is an interactive web interface that lets you visualize and test your endpoints directly from the browser.

. Access the Swagger UI for your Hero service in **Red Hat Developer Hub**:
** Navigate to the `hero-service` component in RHDH
** Click the **Api** tab
+
image::hero-swagger-ui-rhdh.png[align="center",link=self,window=blank,width=600,title="API tab of the hero-service in Red Hat Developer Hub"]

. Select the `$USER-hero` API from the list:
+
image::openapi-provided-rhdh.png[align="center",link=self,window=blank,width=600,title="Selecting the Hero API in the RHDH catalog"]

. Click the **Definition** tab to see the full OpenAPI specification in RHDH.

. Alternatively, access the Swagger UI directly from the application in Dev Mode:
** Navigate to `http://localhost:8080/q/swagger-ui`
+
image::swagger-ui.png[align="center",link=self,window=blank,width=600,title="Interactive Swagger UI for the Hero service -- test your endpoints directly in the browser"]

. Test an endpoint directly from Swagger UI:
** Expand `GET /api/heroes/random`
** Click **Try it out**
** Click **Execute**
** Observe the response with a random hero

=== Verify

✓ The API tab in RHDH displays the Hero service specification

✓ Swagger UI lets you execute GET, POST, PUT, DELETE requests directly from the browser

== Stop Dev Mode

IMPORTANT: Before moving on to the next module, stop Dev Mode to avoid port conflicts.

. In the terminal where Quarkus Dev is running, press `Ctrl + C`.

. Confirm the application shutdown.

== Module summary

**What you accomplished:**

* Accessed the OpenAPI specification automatically generated by Quarkus
* Explored the Hero API from Red Hat Developer Hub via the Api tab
* Interactively tested endpoints with Swagger UI

**Key takeaways:**

* Quarkus automatically generates an OpenAPI 3.0 specification from JAX-RS and Bean Validation annotations
* Swagger UI is included in Dev Mode with no additional configuration
* Red Hat Developer Hub centralizes API documentation for all your components

**Next step:**

Module 5 deploys the Hero service to OpenShift via a **Git commit** and observes the automatic CI/CD pipeline with GitOps.
